content.problemStatement:
With an integer array `nums` and an integer `target`, output all unique quadruplets `[nums[a], nums[b], nums[c], nums[d]]` such that `0 <= a, b, c, d < n`, the indices are distinct, and `nums[a] + nums[b] + nums[c] + nums[d] == target`.

Output the quadruplets in any order. Each quadruplet in the output must be sorted in non-decreasing order and the final list must not contain duplicate quadruplets (the judge will normalize before comparison). Use 64-bit arithmetic for intermediate sums where the language requires it to avoid overflow when elements are near the constraint extremes.

Design an algorithm that is correct and reasonably efficient for `n` up to 200 (expected O(n^3) approach using sorting + two pointers).

notes: The judge normalizes each returned quadruplet by sorting its elements in non-decreasing order and then sorts the list of quadruplets lexicographically before comparing to the expected set. Therefore output ordering is irrelevant.

Generator-style testcases (type = "gen") are expanded by the judge harness at runtime using the described seeds and deterministic procedures. The judge computes expected outputs using a trusted reference implementation (sorting + O(n^3) scan) and compares submission outputs to those values.
Use 64-bit integers for intermediate sums in languages with fixed-width integer types to avoid overflow when elements are near ±1e9.
Solutions must return unique quadruplets only; duplicate quadruplets are considered incorrect.

solution.approach: Sort the array and use two nested loops (i and j) to fix the first two elements, then apply a two-pointer scan (left, right) to find pairs that complete the quadruplet to the target. Skip duplicates at each level (i, j, left, right) to ensure uniqueness. Use 64-bit arithmetic for intermediate sums to avoid overflow when elements are large.

solution.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space (excluding output and sorting overhead)
